name: Configure Resting-State Eyes-Open Alpha Wave Analysis Environment
description:
You are a cognitive neuroscientist preparing a resting-state EEG analysis session for a study on alpha wave dynamics. You have a real EEG baseline recording (eyes-open condition) from PhysioNet that needs to be analyzed.

The OpenBCI GUI is at the System Control Panel. Set up the analysis environment as follows:

- Load the Eyes Open EEG recording in Playback mode: the file is at ~/Documents/OpenBCI_GUI/Recordings/OpenBCI-EEG-S001-EyesOpen.txt
- Add both the Band Power widget (to view brainwave band distributions) and the FFT Plot widget (to see the frequency spectrum with alpha peak) to display panels — both are needed for spectral analysis
- Set the bandpass filter to 1–50 Hz (full spectrum, covering delta through low gamma)
- Set the Time Series vertical scale to 100 µV (appropriate amplitude range for eyes-open alpha)
- Enable Expert Mode
- Capture a screenshot (using 'm' in Expert Mode) to document the analysis setup
- Save the settings configuration

This recording contains real human EEG data (8 channels, 250 Hz) from Subject S001 during eyes-open resting state. The alpha peak (8–12 Hz) should be visible in the FFT Plot, particularly over occipital channels (O1, O2 — channels 7 and 8).

metadata.recording_source: PhysioNet EEGMMI Dataset (eegmmidb 1.0.0), Subject S001, Run R01 (eyes open baseline)
